decisions.reason: As a close-to-core finish variant with low incremental carrying costs, it is sensible to keep it while confirming that demand for black bathroom aesthetics is durable.

This shower channel remains tightly aligned with the firm's architectural drainage capabilities, so the option value of staying in seamless-covering applications still outweighs the limited risk of continuation.
The tileable floor drain fits the firm's barrier-free and design-led core offer, making retention the likely choice unless sales clearly disappoint.
As a complementary design grate with likely modest support and production burden, it is worth keeping on the market while the firm learns its true pull in the premium segment.

Because pump-based drainage is more technically uncertain and a related product was already withdrawn, this newer variant carries a materially higher exit risk, but management would still keep it for now to gather more evidence before abandoning the option.
